generalized_learning.generalized_failure_pattern: A transformation can accidentally treat valid output-domain values as malformed input, while an evidence manifest can similarly self-declare an incomplete vocabulary and appear internally consistent.
generalized_learning.plausible_wrong_implementation: Apply global replacement over an ambiguous character domain, or accept a risk manifest without validating it against an external canonical schema.
trigger_signals: ambiguous replacement input overlaps valid Unicode domain
evidence manifest defines its own family vocabulary
generalized_learning.reusable_control: Use mixed-validity and idempotent sibling tests for transformation domains plus an external canonical-schema validator for evidence manifests before certification.
generalized_learning.prevention_rule: Restrict direct transformations to unambiguous malformed inputs and use lexical/contextual rules for ambiguous visible values; generate evidence vocabulary from the canonical contract rather than local custom labels.
generalized_learning.detection_rule: Test valid output-domain values, mixed inputs, reruns and fail handoff when canonical risk families, applicability reasons, surfaces or control bindings are missing.

transfer_cases.case: A mixed string retains valid characters from the target alphabet while malformed markers are transformed and a rerun is a no-op.
A manifest omitting canonical families is rejected by an external schema validator.

skill_changes.evidence: Delivery prevention requires unambiguous-domain repair and canonical risk-family generation before certification.
Delivery detection includes mixed-validity/idempotency regression coverage and canonical risk-saturation validation.
